findings.title: A local SERVER_NAME marks public WSGI requests as localhost
findings.description: The WSGI middleware passes `SERVER_NAME` as `url_host` to `is_localhost()`. Since `SERVER_NAME` can describe the internal server and any local input makes the helper return true, a deployment with `SERVER_NAME=localhost` or `127.0.0.1` will mark requests as localhost even when `HTTP_HOST` and the client IP are public. If the inbound localhost filter uses this attribute, it can discard production traffic. Use the effective public request host instead, and add a regression test with a local `SERVER_NAME` and public `HTTP_HOST` and client IP.

findings.title: Local SERVER_NAME marks public WSGI requests as localhost
findings.description: In `wsgi.py`, `is_localhost(url_host=environ["SERVER_NAME"])` treats the internal bind name as the request host, so `SERVER_NAME=localhost|127.0.0.1` with a public `HTTP_HOST` still sets `sentry.is_localhost=True` and can drop production traffic via inbound filters. Pass the public host from `get_host(...)` (or omit `url_host` when `HTTP_HOST` is set), and add a regression case with local `SERVER_NAME` + public Host/IP expecting False.

findings.title: Client-controlled X-Forwarded-For forces localhost client_ip
findings.description: is_localhost() uses get_client_ip(), which prefers the first X-Forwarded-For hop with no use_x_forwarded_for gate, so a client can send X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 and get sentry.is_localhost=true. Prefer REMOTE_ADDR unless forwarded headers are explicitly trusted.
